days.title: Lakes and Islands of Plön
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Prinzeninsel
stops.detail: In damp locations that can also be periodically flooded, carr forests dominated by black alders grow, for example, on Lake Großer Plöner See in front of the Prinzeninsel or can be viewed on the Kleiner Warder (Bosau).

stops.name: Halbinsel Störland
stops.detail: Such grazing landscapes exist on the Störland peninsula on the shores of Lake Großer Plöner See, at Lake Barkauer See, at the Middelburg Lakes, or in the Kasseedorfer Teiche nature reserve and surroundings.

stops.name: Heidmoor
stops.detail: In the Heidmoor in the municipality of Seedorf, rewetting measures were carried out and large-scale extensive grazing with cattle was established.

stops.name: Tarbeker Moor
stops.detail: In total, 57 breeding bird species have been recorded in the Tarbeker Moor, including lapwing, garganey, red-necked grebe, little ringed plover, woodlark, and crane.

stops.name: Bungsberg
stops.detail: It extends in a north-south direction from Lake Selenter See to the town of Bad Segeberg and in a west-east direction from Ascheberg at Lake Großer Plöner See to Schönwalde at Bungsberg.
